output.description: Trust Fabric is bought by large enterprises and regulated organisations - spanning SaaS, online retail, fintech, automotive, energy, pharma, gaming, media, travel, telecoms and public sector - that run production Kubernetes with distributed, many-service architectures managed by an in-house engineering team. These buyers are based in North America, the UK and Ireland, or Continental Europe, and range from roughly 501 employees up to large global enterprises of around 50,000 staff. The purchase is decided by the platform, infrastructure or security leader who owns the cluster and its certificate estate, typically the CTO, CIO, CISO or a VP, Director or Head of Engineering, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, SRE, DevOps or Security.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor in the certificate-lifecycle management space sells to enterprise security and PKI teams who need to automate certificate issuance and renewal, regardless of whether their infrastructure runs on Kubernetes at scale.

buyer.rubric: Buyers are the platform, infrastructure or security leader who owns the Kubernetes cluster and its certificate estate: CTO, CIO, CISO, and the VP, Director or Head of Engineering, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Security Engineering, Information Security or Architecture, with the CEO qualifying only at companies under about 1,000 employees. Titles that carry a senior title but never buy this include the CFO, CMO, CRO, VP of Sales, VP of Marketing, and other commercial, HR or finance leaders.

requirements.text: The company runs production Kubernetes with a distributed architecture or many independent services.

The company operates its own infrastructure with an in-house engineering team rather than being an outsourced platform, MSP, systems integrator, consultancy, agency, private equity firm, recruiter, freelancer, or certificate-lifecycle vendor such as AppViewX, Entrust or CyberArk.
The company has between 501 and 50,000 employees.
The company's operations are uptime-critical or regulated such that an hour of downtime would be a board-level event.
The company is based in North America, the UK and Ireland, or Continental Europe.

The company shows a live buying signal such as a platform, SRE, infrastructure or PKI role posted in the last 30 days naming Kubernetes, TLS, mTLS, cert-manager, PKI or service mesh; public evidence of production Kubernetes at scale; a published SLA; DORA, PSD2, NIS2 or PCI DSS obligations; a new platform or security leader appointed in the last 12 months; a post-quantum commitment; or a public certificate or TLS incident in the last 90 days.
